title: 'Lakshmi Aa Rahi Hai': When Diljit Dosanjh Turned a Chicago Concert Into a Gender Reveal Party
excerpt: Midway through the sold-out opening night of his Aura World Tour, the Punjabi superstar paused to announce an NRI couple's baby — and the internet lost its collective mind.
body:
Halfway through his sold-out show at Chicago's Allstate Arena, Diljit Dosanjh did something no one in the 18,000-strong crowd saw coming. He paused mid-set, called an expecting couple to the front, and held up a poster that read: **'Lakshmi Aa Rahi Hai'** — It's a girl.

The arena erupted. The couple — Indian-Americans who'd driven from Michigan for the show — burst into tears. And Diljit, in typical Diljit fashion, grinned, said "Balle balle," and launched straight into 'Born to Shine.'

## The Aura Tour Is a Diaspora Event

The May 10 Chicago concert wasn't just a gig. It was the opening night of the North American leg of Diljit's **Aura World Tour 2026**, a 13-city run through Dallas, Nashville, Atlanta, Orlando, New York (Madison Square Garden), Los Angeles, San Francisco, and Toronto. Tickets for most stops sold out within hours of going live — a feat that would have been unimaginable for a Punjabi artist even five years ago.

What makes Diljit's tour different from any other Indian artist playing arenas in America is the audience composition. These aren't nostalgia crowds of first-generation uncles and aunties. The front rows at Allstate Arena were packed with second-generation Indian-Americans in their twenties and thirties — kids who grew up on Drake and Dua Lipa but now wear 'G.O.A.T.' hoodies and know every lyric to 'Lover.'

## More Than Music

The gender reveal moment has now racked up millions of views across Instagram and YouTube, with fans calling it 'pure,' 'adorable,' and 'the most Punjabi thing ever.' But the clip is resonant for a deeper reason: it captures the way Diljit has become something more than a pop star for the diaspora. He's a bridge — between the Punjab their parents left and the America they grew up in, between Bhangra and Billboard, between reverence for tradition and unabashed global ambition.

Earlier in the tour, Diljit had addressed a separate controversy — pro-Khalistan flags spotted at a Canadian concert date — with characteristic directness: "If you abuse my fans, it will not be tolerated." He later clarified he had no objection to any flags but prioritised his audience's safety above politics.

## The 31-Song Set

The Aura Tour set spans 31 tracks, opening with 'G.O.A.T.' and including a tribute section dedicated to the late Amar Singh Chamkila, the legendary Punjabi artist whose life Diljit portrayed in the 2024 Netflix biopic. The production — massive LED walls, pyro, live Bhangra dancers — is at a level Indian touring acts have rarely attempted in North American venues.

## What's Next

Diljit's American momentum isn't slowing. His next film, **'Main Vaapas Aaunga'**, is set for a June 12 global release. The tour continues through Dallas (May 16), Nashville, Atlanta, New York's Madison Square Garden, and wraps in Toronto in June. For the millions of NRIs who've followed his rise from Jalandhar to Jimmy Fallon's couch, the Chicago gender reveal was just the latest proof that Punjabi pop has arrived — not at the margins, but at the center.

**Where to catch Diljit live:** Remaining tour dates across the US and Canada are available on Ticketmaster. Most stops are at 18,000+ capacity arenas.
